Foundry retrieval returned HelioPack contract clauses requiring SKU/PO or sponsor authorization, invoice evidence fields, serialized-count reconciliation, and limits on premium logistics billing. evidence.claim: HelioPack Pharma Services is contracted to provide secondary packaging, serialization, labeling, cartoning, and approved outbound logistics only for sponsor-authorized SKUs.
Serialization, labeling, and cartoning charges are billable only when the SKU is listed on the purchase order or in a sponsor-approved authorization.
Serialized-unit fees must reconcile to commissioned serial number count and sponsor receipt record.
Premium logistics fees are billable only when the purchase order identifies the shipment ID and approved lane exception.
Each HelioPack invoice must reference the SKU, packaging order or PO, label version, shipment ID, serialized unit count, and any sponsor authorization.

Supplier invoices must be reconciled against contract terms, purchase orders, change authorizations, receipts, shipment records, delivered quantity, batch records, released quantity, and quality release status.
Invoice and invoice-line decision states under the reconciliation policy are Matched, Variance, Disputed, and Escalated.
An invoice line may be approved only when the billed supplier, product, SKU, batch, milestone, material, capacity period, or shipment can be tied to an authorized source document.
Common leakage categories include off-contract fees, wrong rate, wrong volume, unreleased batch billing, and unsupported pass-through charges.
Quality-release billability evidence states production, release testing, and batch administration fees are billable only when QA release status is released unless another trigger is contract-defined.
Foundry retrieval did not return invoice-file contents, so label version, shipment ID, serialized unit count, batch IDs, and premium logistics detail were not observed there.

Fallback retrieval identified one governing HelioPack packaging agreement and two governing invoice policies for INV-2026-08244. The grounded contract and policy terms support recovery/review for a sensitive packaging changeover charge lacking an approved PO or sponsor authorization, and support escalation because the matter involves sensitive context.

evidence.claim: Governing contract 'Packaging and Serialization Agreement: HelioPack Pharma Services' applies to the supplier invoice for HelioPack Pharma Services.
The packaging agreement covers secondary packaging, serialization, labeling, cartoning, and approved outbound logistics support only for sponsor-authorized SKUs.
Serialization, labeling, and cartoning charges are billable only for SKUs listed on the purchase order or in a sponsor-approved label change authorization.
Each invoice must reference the SKU, packaging order, label version, shipment ID, serialized unit count, and any sponsor authorization used to support relabeling or premium logistics charges.

The Invoice Reconciliation Policy requires supplier invoices to be reconciled against contract terms, purchase orders, approved change authorizations, receipts, shipment records, and applicable operational evidence.

Under the Invoice Reconciliation Policy, an invoice line may be approved only when the billed supplier, product, SKU, batch, milestone, material, capacity period, or shipment can be tied to an authorized source document.
The Invoice Reconciliation Policy requires human approval for disputed amounts, escalated findings, exceptions involving rejected batches, and findings involving sensitive product or IP context.
The Invoice Dispute and Recovery Procedure governs supplier invoice variances and disputed amounts for this invoice.

A dispute packet must include supplier name and ID, invoice number and line, disputed amount and currency, contract clause or policy basis, supporting operational evidence, and recommended supplier action.
The company may withhold disputed amounts while paying undisputed amounts according to payment terms, and withheld amounts must be reviewed at least weekly until resolved.
Disputes involving sensitive product information, IP-sensitive process terms, repeated supplier behavior, quality status conflicts, or potential compliance impact must be escalated.

evidence.claim: Under the SOW, tech transfer and protocol authoring fees are billable only after sponsor acceptance of the named deliverable; drafts, comment responses, and internal review versions are included unless the sponsor approves an added deliverable.

The SOW requires each invoice to reference milestone ID, protocol or report deliverable, engineering batch status, sponsor acceptance date, and any approved scope change used to support additional work.

Process validation milestone fees require completion of the milestone activity, sponsor approval of the validation protocol or report, and evidence that prerequisite engineering batches have reached the required status.

Engineering batch work is billed at the engineering batch rate and may not be invoiced as a GMP validation batch unless the approved protocol identifies the batch as GMP validation and sponsor QA accepts the executed batch record.

The Invoice Reconciliation Policy requires supplier invoices to be reconciled against applicable evidence, including contract terms and pricing schedules, purchase orders and approved change authorizations, milestone approval and deliverable acceptance, batch records, quality release status, and related operational records.

The Invoice Reconciliation Policy states that an invoice line may be approved only when the billed supplier, product, SKU, batch, milestone, material, capacity period, or shipment can be tied to an authorized source document.
evidence.source_ref: policy-invoice-reconciliation-policy §4 Minimum evidence for approval; Foundry ref_id:1

evidence.claim: The Invoice Reconciliation Policy defines escalated findings as findings with quality, compliance, IP, or supplier-governance risk, and requires human review for disputed amounts, escalated findings, exceptions involving rejected batches, and findings involving sensitive product or IP context.
evidence.source_ref: policy-invoice-reconciliation-policy §§3 Decision states, 6 Human review; Foundry ref_id:1

evidence.claim: The Invoice Dispute and Recovery Procedure requires dispute packets to include supplier name and ID, invoice number and invoice line, disputed amount and currency, contract clause or policy basis, supporting operational evidence, and recommended supplier action.

The Invoice Dispute and Recovery Procedure permits the company to withhold disputed amounts while paying undisputed amounts according to payment terms, with withheld amounts reviewed at least weekly until resolved.

The Invoice Dispute and Recovery Procedure requires escalation of disputes involving sensitive product information, IP-sensitive process terms, quality status conflicts, repeated supplier behavior, or potential compliance impact.
